sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Vision Statement**: Captalizes on the motto **'Creative India; Innovative India'** to integrate IPRs as a policy driver for economic, social, and cultural development.
• **Nodal Agency**: Administered under the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
• **Seven Pillars**: Built around seven core objectives: IPR Awareness, Generation of IPRs, Legal and Legislative Framework, Administration and Management, Commercialization of IPR, Enforcement and Adjudication, and Human Capital Development.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Aligns India's domestic legal regime fully with the **World Trade Organization's (WTO) TRIPS Agreement** while safeguarding national public health priorities and traditional knowledge.

items.term: CGPDTM (Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks)
items.definition: The overarching statutory office under DPIIT responsible for administering Patents, Trademarks, Designs, and Geographical Indications in India.

items.term: CIPAM (Cell for IPR Promotion and Management)
items.definition: A professional body operating under DPIIT created to facilitate implementation of the National IPR Policy, spread awareness, and streamline IP commercialization.
A pioneering Indian repository of traditional medicinal knowledge established to prevent the bio-piracy and wrongful grant of patents on Indian systems of medicine.

A statutory mechanism under Section 92 of the Patents Act allowing governments to authorize production of a patented drug/invention by domestic generic players without patentee consent during national emergencies.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Patent Offices**: Located in Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, and Chennai, with the Head Office of CGPDTM in Mumbai.
• **GI Hubs**: High concentration of registered GIs in Southern states (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala) and North-Eastern states, spanning handicrafts, agricultural goods, and manufactured items.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Backlog of patent and trademark applications, lack of grassroots awareness among MSMEs, and enforcement challenges against counterfeiting.
• **Policy Interventions**: Digitalization of IP offices, fee reductions for Startups, MSMEs, and women entrepreneurs, and strengthening commercial courts for IP disputes.

items.title: Mnemonic for Seven Pillars of National IPR Policy
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'AGL-ACHE' (Awareness, Generation, Legal, Administration, Commercialization, Human Capital, Enforcement).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Covers the 7 strategic pillars outlined in the 2016 IPR Policy framework.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly identifies statements in MCQs testing whether specific developmental areas fall under the policy.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember 'DPIIT' as the parent ministry and '2016' as the launch year for all policy-related chronological questions.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently misleads candidates by stating that the National IPR Policy is framed or enforced directly by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO). Remember, it is a domestic policy formulated by the Government of India (DPIIT), though it complies with international obligations like TRIPS.

Mains Value Addition: In answers concerning innovation and 'Make in India', emphasize how balancing robust IP protection with flexibilities like Section 3(d) of the Patents Act ensures affordable healthcare and promotes indigenous R&D.

keyTakeaways: The National IPR Policy 2016 operates under the guiding framework of 'Creative India; Innovative India' steered by DPIIT.
It balances strict IP enforcement with public welfare safeguards such as compulsory licensing and protection of traditional knowledge via TKDL.
Institutional streamlining through CIPAM and digitisation of patent/trademark offices have drastically improved India's Global Innovation Index (GII) ranking.
